title: Panthers Sign Cam Gill After Nic Scourton’s Torn ACL Devastates Training Camp Opener
excerpt: Carolina’s second-year edge rusher is out for the 2026 season after going down on Day 1, prompting the NFC South champions to bring back a UFL Defensive Player of the Year.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Nic Scourton tore his ACL and will miss the entire 2026 season.
  • Cam Gill, UFL's 2026 Defensive Player of the Year, has been signed by the Panthers.
  • Scourton had 47 tackles and 5 sacks in his rookie season.
  • The Panthers also have Patrick Jones II and Princely Umanmielen as backup edge rushers.
  • Gill previously played for the Panthers in 2024, recording 22 tackles.

  • Nic Scourton tore his ACL during the Panthers' training camp opener and will miss the entire 2026 NFL season.
  • The Panthers signed outside linebacker Cam Gill to bolster their pass rush following Scourton's injury.
  • Scourton was a second-round draft pick in 2025 and had a strong rookie season with 47 tackles and 5 sacks.
  • Cam Gill returns to the Panthers after leading the UFL in sacks and being named the league's Defensive Player of the Year.

The Carolina Panthers’ first day of training camp ended with their most feared outcome. Second-year edge rusher Nic Scourton tore his ACL during team drills on a wet field Thursday morning and will miss the entire 2026 NFL season, the team confirmed after an MRI.

Within hours, the reigning NFC South champions moved to shore up their pass rush. Carolina agreed to terms with outside linebacker Cam Gill, according to Fox Sports’ Greg Auman — a familiar face returning to a defense that now faces a significant test of depth.

A Devastating Blow

Scourton, 21, went down late in the opening practice session while engaged in a block with an offensive lineman. Players immediately gathered around him on one knee in what reporters described as a “grim scene.” Scourton held his hand over his face as he was placed on a cart.

https://x.com/gregauman/status/2080327505978720427

Before he left the field, head coach Dave Canales and every player on the roster walked over individually to embrace him.

“Whenever you’re in a group of people doing something hard together, it has a way of creating a special bond. I’m proud of that.”

— Dave Canales, Panthers Head Coach

Scourton was Carolina’s 2025 second-round draft pick out of Texas A&M, where he earned first-team All-SEC honors. He made an immediate impact as a rookie, playing all 17 games with eight starts and finishing with 47 tackles, 5 sacks, and 9 quarterback hits. He had been projected to start alongside free-agent acquisition Jaelan Phillips this season.

Gill Brings UFL Pedigree

Gill, 28, returns to Carolina after a standout spring in the United Football League. Playing for the Louisville Kings, he recorded a league-leading 11 sacks in 10 games and was named the UFL’s 2026 Defensive Player of the Year.

The Sumter, South Carolina native and Wagner College product has NFL experience on his resume. He won Super Bowl LV as a rookie with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2021, contributing a half-sack and a forced fumble on Patrick Mahomes in the championship game. He played for the Panthers in 2024, recording 22 tackles in 10 games.

Across 50 career regular-season NFL games with the Buccaneers and Panthers, Gill has totaled 51 tackles and 2.5 sacks.

Depth Will Be Tested

Beyond Gill, the Panthers will look to sixth-year veteran Patrick Jones II and 2025 third-round pick Princely Umanmielen to absorb the workload. Edge rushers Trevis Gipson, Nick Hampton, Thomas Incoom, and undrafted rookie Isaiah Smith round out the position group.

Quarterback Bryce Young, who was near the play when Scourton went down, praised his teammate’s development. “He has a super-high motor, has great energy. He’s fun to be around. He has raised the level of practice many times,” Young said.

Canales expressed confidence in the roster’s ability to absorb the loss. “We’ve got depth. That’s why we keep bringing in guys. We have guys that we trust,” he said.

The Panthers enter 2026 as NFC South champions looking to build on a breakthrough 2025 campaign. Losing Scourton is a significant setback, but the speed of Gill’s signing suggests the front office was prepared for contingencies.
